FIB_PLUS	<p>0d36_d104</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e11;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #874e11;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e11;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7140ad;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7140ad;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7140ad;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, npx, +++, npx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". For example, if the distance is fifty one centimorgans, simply write "51".</li><li><i>Important Tip 3:</i> Your gene order answer should be written as three letters only, with no spaces, commas, hyphens, or other characters allowed. Once calculated, fill in the following four blanks: </p><ul><li>The distance between genes K and W is [KW] cM (KW)</li><li>The distance between genes K and Y is [KY] cM (KY)</li><li>The distance between genes W and Y is [WY] cM (WY)</li><li>From this, the correct order of the genes is [geneorder] (gene order).</li></ul><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Pick any two genes and assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and pick a new pair of genes until all pairs are complete.</li></ul><h6>Important Answer Guidelines</h6><p><ul><li><i>Important Tip 1:</i> Your calculated distances between each pair of genes should be a whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". For example, if the distance is fifty one centimorgans, simply write "51".</li><li><i>Important Tip 3:</i> Your gene order answer should be written as three letters only, with no spaces, commas, hyphens, or other characters allowed. FIB_PLUS	<p>7198_9d25</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a22d3d;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a22d3d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a22d3d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2a5da6;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #2a5da6;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. Once calculated, fill in the following four blanks: </p><ul><li>The distance between genes B and K is [BK] cM (BK)</li><li>The distance between genes B and X is [BX] cM (BX)</li><li>The distance between genes K and X is [KX] cM (KX)</li><li>From this, the correct order of the genes is [geneorder] (gene order).</li></ul><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Pick any two genes and assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and pick a new pair of genes until all pairs are complete.</li></ul><h6>Important Answer Guidelines</h6><p><ul><li><i>Important Tip 1:</i> Your calculated distances between each pair of genes should be a whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". FIB_PLUS	<p>c6d7_053d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e11;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #874e11;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e11;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687a;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #17687a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687a;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7140ad;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7140ad;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7140ad;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ahm, +++, ahm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Once calculated, fill in the following four blanks: </p><ul><li>The distance between genes E and F is [EF] cM (EF)</li><li>The distance between genes E and X is [EX] cM (EX)</li><li>The distance between genes F and X is [FX] cM (FX)</li><li>From this, the correct order of the genes is [geneorder] (gene order).</li></ul><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Pick any two genes and assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and pick a new pair of genes until all pairs are complete.</li></ul><h6>Important Answer Guidelines</h6><p><ul><li><i>Important Tip 1:</i> Your calculated distances between each pair of genes should be a whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". For example, if the distance is fifty one centimorgans, simply write "51".</li><li><i>Important Tip 3:</i> Your gene order answer should be written as three letters only, with no spaces, commas, hyphens, or other characters allowed. FIB_PLUS	<p>0518_1a23</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e11;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #874e11;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e11;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0b7132;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #0b7132;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0b7132;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7140ad;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7140ad;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. Once calculated, fill in the following four blanks: </p><ul><li>The distance between genes A and J is [AJ] cM (AJ)</li><li>The distance between genes A and N is [AN] cM (AN)</li><li>The distance between genes J and N is [JN] cM (JN)</li><li>From this, the correct order of the genes is [geneorder] (gene order).</li></ul><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Pick any two genes and assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and pick a new pair of genes until all pairs are complete.</li></ul><h6>Important Answer Guidelines</h6><p><ul><li><i>Important Tip 1:</i> Your calculated distances between each pair of genes should be a whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". For example, if the distance is fifty one centimorgans, simply write "51".</li><li><i>Important Tip 3:</i> Your gene order answer should be written as three letters only, with no spaces, commas, hyphens, or other characters allowed. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3292;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8b3292;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>0b4c_8716</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a22d3d;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a22d3d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a22d3d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #666016;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #666016;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666016;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687a;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #17687a;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687a;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, emn, +++, emn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Once calculated, fill in the following four blanks: </p><ul><li>The distance between genes E and N is [EN] cM (EN)</li><li>The distance between genes E and W is [EW] cM (EW)</li><li>The distance between genes N and W is [NW] cM (NW)</li><li>From this, the correct order of the genes is [geneorder] (gene order).</li></ul><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Pick any two genes and assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and pick a new pair of genes until all pairs are complete.</li></ul><h6>Important Answer Guidelines</h6><p><ul><li><i>Important Tip 1:</i> Your calculated distances between each pair of genes should be a whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units".
